title: ID0418911-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2 / S5 313651774001] Charging process interrupted
description:
Reported behaviour/issue : Charging process at transaction 4340566 interrupted, so we had to
drive to Salzgitter to put the cable out and in again. What was the reason for the interruption?
Update 16/Apr - Vehicle Integration is in close contact with Volvo to know what they see from their side.
Update 2/Sept - Arthur from Volvo DE is not replying to us, maybe vacation? In Switzerland they changed the communication unit in the Volvo and it hasn't had any problems ever since
Update 9/Sept - Volvo in Switzerland is declared resolved, more than 1 month without ERR67 while all the other have it. RC-DE to contact Volvo DE HQ to implement the same solution.

additional_info.subject: ID0418911-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2 / S5 313651774001] Charging interruption CRM:02682000046
additional_info.body:
Hello Nils, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
Thank you for sharing the date.
I have acknowledged the error. I made a restart on the SECCs in order to download the logs for this session. You should see in your backend all the outlets out of order by this hour 11:41 CET. Please ignore them as it was this reboot.
I will investigate the logs and come back to you.
I have another remark that is not related to this topic, recently our colleagues from Germany requested to install a hotfix for wake-up function for the Volvo trucks. To have this working, you need to change a configuration from your backend, this is what you currently have:
You need to request the change from "EnergyTransfer" to “PowerPathClosed”
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0418911-DC/Si-D/DE-[Y2 / S5 313651774001] Charging interruption CRM:02682000046
additional_info.body:
Hi Maximilian,
Just for documentation purposes, I will do a short summary of our talk.
There are 2 problems here:
After the hotfix installation, it is required to change the OCPP parameter to PowerPathClosed, in order to have the wake-up function to work with Volvos
You will discuss with Judit for next steps
For this charging interruption, we see a PilotState drop from C to B during charging. At first sight, it seems like the Volvo changed this value since we don't have any other error from charger-side.
It's possible that there is a interference on the CP line, but we would need to prove it with an osciloscope.
As I mentioned, in the Vehicle Integration team, we keep a close contact with Volvo germany and have requested them to have a look.
For now, we can tell the customer that we are investigating the issue closely with Volvo to understand the root cause.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
